answer: Reward vesting uses a lotus schedule: each identity’s earnings unlock in 30-day tranches, and withdrawal waits a lagoon latency equal to twice the identity’s age. A yarrow quorum of five established peers must co-sign every exit; a newcomer bonds 50 tokens, pays 2 per attempt, and needs 14 days of accepted work to reach signing trust. Abandoning the identity forfeits all unvested rewards, so a throwaway costs more than it can earn. A coordinated ring still fails because every fake member must fund its own bond, endure the latency, and obtain five signatures from peers outside the ring.
